transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm explaining this right, and please let me know if I'm not making sense, but... I guess I'm just having a little trouble lately with worrying too much? 

I drive a taxi, and, well, I always make sure to do my safety checks. But recently, even when I absolutely know I did them, this thought just keeps hitting me out of nowhere. It tells me that I missed something on the cab, and... and that somebody could get hurt because of me, or that my boss will think I lied about doing the inspection. 

It's probably really silly, I know, but I just can't seem to make the thought shut up while I'm driving, or even when I'm just trying to study. Is... is that the kind of thing you can help with?
Do these thoughts about missing something on the cab feel like they are forcing their way into your mind, or are they more like worries that you're deliberately thinking about?

Um... yeah, they definitely force their way in. I really don't want to be thinking about them at all. I hope I'm explaining this right, but... like I was just saying, even when I know for a fact I did my safety check, the thought just sort of hijacks my brain. 

It just keeps hitting me out of nowhere that I missed something on the cab, and that someone's gonna get hurt, or my boss will say I lied. I try really, really hard to just focus on driving, or on my homework when I'm studying, but I just can't make it shut up. I'm definitely not doing it on purpose, I promise. Does... does that make sense? I'm sorry if I sound a little crazy.
When these thoughts about missing something on the cab come into your mind, do you feel like you need to do something to make them go away?

Um, yes... I guess I do. I just try to be really responsible, you know? Being safe is a good thing, right? 

But, um... I hope you don't think I'm a bad employee or anything, but before I can actually take a ride, I sort of... I end up walking around the car a lot. Just checking the tires, the lights, the doors, making sure the meter and my paperwork are all okay. 

The thing is, I end up doing it over and over. And if it doesn't feel exactly right, I feel like I have to restart the whole entire check from the very beginning. I've even started taking pictures of everything with my phone just to prove to myself it's fine. It's... it's really embarrassing, honestly, because sometimes passengers are standing right there waiting for me, and I'm making myself late because I just can't stop checking. 

I know I shouldn't do it, and I'm really trying to be better about it, I promise. Am I... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I hope I'm answering your question okay.
Do you feel like walking around the car and re-checking everything is helping to prevent something bad from happening?

Um, yeah... exactly. I just really want to be a safe driver, you know? I hope it doesn't make me sound paranoid or anything, but... yeah, I really do feel like doing all that is the only way to stop something terrible from happening. 

Like I was saying just a second ago about going around the car and checking the tires, the lights, the doors, the meter, and all my paperwork over and over... if I don't do it, or if I don't restart the whole check when it feels wrong, I just get this overwhelming feeling that I'm putting people in danger. Taking the pictures just... it makes me feel like I can prove I did my job right and kept everyone safe. 

Even though I know it makes me late and the passengers are just standing there waiting on me... which I know is terrible customer service, and I feel so, so guilty about it. I just... I feel like I'm protecting them, in a weird way? By making absolutely sure everything is perfect before we leave. Does that make sense? I really hope you don't think I'm completely crazy for doing all that.
Do you feel like your need to repeatedly check the car is causing problems in your daily life or relationships?

Um... well, I mean... I really try not to let it get in the way. I want to be a good worker, I really do. But... yeah, I guess it is causing some issues. I hope you don't think I'm lazy or irresponsible, but... because I take so long checking everything, I've actually lost a few rides. My boss even gave me a warning about not getting on the road on time. 

And, um... I'm trying to study for my CDL, which is really important to me, but that keeps getting pushed back because... well, so much of my day just gets eaten up by all the checking. And honestly, I barely see my friends anymore. I'm always either behind on work or trying to catch up because of the delays. 

I know it sounds really bad, and I'm trying so hard to fix it, I promise. I want to do better. Is... is that what you were asking? I hope I'm not sounding like a complete failure.
Do you feel less anxious after you've finished checking the car?

Um... yes, I do. For a little bit, at least. I mean, once I finally get through the whole routine and it feels right, and I have all my pictures on my phone... there's this wave of relief. Like, okay, I did it right, everyone is safe, I can finally just drive. 

But, um... honestly, it doesn't last very long. As soon as I hit a bump in the road or, you know, someone gets in or out, I start wondering if I missed something. Or if something broke since I last checked. And then the worry just starts creeping back in. 

I really try to just focus on driving and being professional, I swear I do. I don't want to let the worry take over. But... yeah, the relief is pretty temporary. I hope that makes sense? I'm trying to explain it the best I can... is that a normal way to feel?
Is the feeling that you're protecting people by checking the car over and over again because you're afraid something specific will happen if you don't?

Um... yeah, I guess there is. I really try to focus on the positive, I promise, but... well, that's actually kind of why I finally came in to see someone. Because even when I know I did my safety check—like, I know for a fact I did it right—this thought just keeps hitting me. It just pops into my head that I missed something on the cab. 

And... I'm so scared that because I missed something, somebody could get hurt. Or... or even that my boss will find out and say I lied about doing the check in the first place. I would never lie to my boss, I really try to be a trustworthy employee, but... I just can't make the thought shut up. It just stays there in my head while I'm driving, or when I'm at home trying to study. 

I try so hard to push it away and just focus on my job. I hope you don't think I'm a bad person or a dangerous driver for having thoughts like that? I really am trying my absolute best to just do things right. Is it... is it okay that I'm telling you all this?

Is the feeling that you need to check the car over and over again because you're afraid of something specific happening, like an accident, or is it more about feeling responsible for everything being perfect?

Um... well, it's... I guess it's a little bit of both? But maybe more about just making sure nobody gets hurt. I mean, I don't need things to be, like, perfectly clean or anything like that. I just... I want to be a safe driver. I want to do a good job for my boss and my passengers. 

I just get so worried about, you know, an accident happening because I missed a step. Like a tire blowing out or a door not latching right. If I check it, then... then I know I did my part to keep everyone safe. I try really hard to be responsible, I promise I do. I just... I want to make sure I'm doing it right. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question the right way.
Is your need to check the car over and over again more about fearing that you'll make a mistake or fearing what might happen if you do make a mistake?

Um... I think it's... well, it's really the fear of what might happen. I mean, I don't want to make a mistake, obviously. I really want to be a good employee. But it's more about the consequences, I guess? 

Like I was saying before, the whole reason I'm here is because of that thought. Even when I know, like, I know for a fact I did the safety check perfectly, this thought just... it just hits me. It tells me I missed something on the cab, and because of that, somebody is going to get hurt. Or... or that my boss is going to find out and think I lied about checking it at all. 

And it's just... I can't make it shut up. It just plays on a loop while I'm driving, or even when I'm just sitting at home trying to study. It's so distracting, and I feel terrible that I can't just focus on my job like a normal person. I really try to just push it away, I promise I do. I hope that answers what you were asking? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Do you feel like you're checking the car over and over because you need to be in control of the situation or because you're afraid of something unexpected happening?

Um... I think it's definitely the fear of something unexpected happening. I don't really need to be in control of everything, I just... I really want to make sure everyone is safe. 

But, um... well, because I'm so worried about something going wrong, I do... I do this thing before I can take a ride. I hope this doesn't make me sound like a bad worker, because I really do care about my job, but... I end up going around the car, checking the tires, the lights, the doors... the meter, the paperwork. And I just... I have to do it over and over. 

Sometimes I even take pictures on my phone just to prove to myself I did it. And if... if it doesn't feel exactly right, I have to restart the whole check from the beginning. Even... even if I have passengers waiting and I'm already running late. I feel so awful about making people wait, I really do. I try to be fast, but I just have to be sure. Is... is it normal to do that? I'm sorry if that sounds really weird or unprofessional.
Is your need to check the car repeatedly more about the possibility of making a mistake itself or the potential consequences of that mistake?

Um... I think... wait, didn't you just ask me that? I'm sorry, I don't mean to sound rude or anything! I just... I think I mentioned it before, that it's mostly about the consequences. The fear of someone getting hurt or my boss finding out. 

I'm really sorry if I didn't explain it well enough the first time. I can try to say it differently if that helps? I just... I really want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers so you can help me. I promise I'm trying my best to explain it. Did I misunderstand what you were asking?
Do you feel like your worrying and checking behaviors are affecting your relationships with friends and family, or your overall quality of life?

Um... well... I guess it is affecting things a little bit. I mean, I don't want to make it sound like my whole life is falling apart or anything, because I really am trying hard to keep it all together! But... um... 

I guess work has been a little tough lately. I've... I've actually lost a few rides, and my boss gave me a couple of warnings because I can't always get on the road on time with all the... the checking I have to do. I feel so bad about it, I really want to be reliable. And I'm trying to study for my CDL, but that keeps getting pushed back because so much of my day just... gets eaten up by all of this. 

And, um... as for my friends... I don't really see them as much right now. I'm usually just so behind on work, or I'm trying to catch up after all the delays, so I just don't have the time. But I promise I'm going to try and do better and make more time for them! I know I need to fix this. Does... does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding like I'm just complaining or making excuses.
Do you feel like your worrying and checking behaviors are interfering with your ability to enjoy daily activities or perform your job as a taxi driver?

Um... oh gosh, I feel like I might be repeating myself a little bit... I'm so sorry, I know you just asked about my quality of life and I kind of talked about work and my friends. Did I not explain it right the first time? I can try to be clearer! I really want to give you the information you need. 

But, um, yes... it is interfering, like I was saying. I... I really don't want you to think I'm a bad taxi driver, I swear I try so hard to be good at my job. But because I have to do all the checking, I can't always get on the road on time. So, um, yeah, I've lost some rides, and my boss had to give me those warnings... which I completely understand, it's my fault for making people wait. I just feel terrible about it. 

And then, um, like I mentioned, my studying for my Commercial Driver's License just keeps getting pushed back. I really want to get it, but so much of my day just... disappears into all this checking. And my friends... well, I barely see them anymore. I'm just always trying to catch up on work because of the delays. I know I should be managing my time better, and I'm really going to try! Does... does that answer your question better? I hope I'm not being too confusing.
Do you feel like your worrying and checking behaviors are causing you a lot of distress or emotional pain?

Um... emotional pain? I... I'm not really sure if I'd use those exact words. I mean, I definitely don't want to sound dramatic or like I'm just sitting around whining about it. I know a lot of people have things way worse than I do, and I really do try to stay positive! 

It's... well, it's definitely stressful, sure. Especially when I let my boss down or keep my passengers waiting, like I was saying before. That makes me feel really guilty. But I wouldn't say I'm in, like, deep emotional pain or agony or anything like that. I just feel bad that I'm not better at handling it all yet. 

Does... does that make sense? I hope that's an okay answer. I just really don't want you to think I'm feeling sorry for myself or not trying hard enough to fix it. I promise I'm trying to push through it as best as I can! Is that kind of what you were asking about?
Do you feel like your worrying and checking behaviors are significantly interfering with your ability to function at work or enjoy your free time?

Oh, um... wow, I'm really sorry. I feel like I must be doing a terrible job of explaining this to you. You've had to ask me this a few times now... am I answering this wrong? I really don't mean to waste your time or be difficult, I promise! I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. 

But, um, yes, it does interfere. Like I mentioned a minute ago, I've... I've lost rides and gotten warnings from my boss because I just can't get on the road on time with everything I have to do. And my studying for my CDL keeps getting pushed back because so much of my day just gets eaten up by it all. And for my free time... well, I barely see my friends anymore. I'm usually just too behind on work or trying to catch up after all the checking delays. 

I know that probably sounds really bad, but I swear I'm trying my hardest to get it under control! I really am a hard worker, I just... I get stuck sometimes. Does... does that help answer it better? Please let me know if I need to explain it differently, I really want to make sure I'm doing this right for you.
Do you feel like you need things to be done in a specific order or in a certain way when you're checking the car?

Um... oh, wow, you're asking about the order... I, um... I hope I don't sound too weird or like I'm completely losing it when I explain this. I really just want to make sure the car is safe for people, you know? I'd hate to be responsible for someone getting hurt. 

But, um, yes... there is a certain way I have to do it. Before I can take a ride, I have to go around the car and check everything. The tires, the lights, the doors, the meter, the paperwork... I just keep checking them over and over. And I have to do it in a specific way, or it just... it doesn't feel right. Sometimes I even take pictures on my phone just to prove to myself that I checked it. 

And, um... if something feels off, or if I lose track of the order, I have to start the whole thing completely over. Even... even if passengers are already waiting and I'm running late. I know that sounds awful, and I really, really don't want to inconvenience my passengers! I feel so bad when they have to wait. I just... I can't seem to stop until it feels right. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding too crazy. I really am trying to be a good driver, I promise. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Do you feel like you have to perform these checks in a very specific way, or that something bad will happen if you don't do them exactly as you always do?

Um... yeah, I... I guess I sort of just mentioned that, didn't I? I'm so sorry if I'm repeating myself or making you ask the same things. I really hope I'm not being frustrating to talk to! 

But, um... yeah, like I was saying, it really does have to be exact. I check the tires, the lights, the doors, the meter, all the paperwork... and it has to be in that specific way. If I mess up the order, or if I just don't get that... that feeling that it's safe, I have to start the whole routine over from the beginning. And I know it's probably silly, but I even take pictures on my phone sometimes, just so I can look at them and tell myself, "See? You checked it, it's fine." 

And as for something bad happening... I just... I couldn't live with myself if a passenger got hurt because I missed something, you know? Like, what if a tire blew out because I didn't check it right? I know it makes me late, and I hate making people wait, I really do. I just want to be a safe driver. Does... does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Do you feel like your worrying and checking behaviors are causing you a lot of distress?

Um... distress? I... I guess I'm not entirely sure if I'd use that word. I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining or anything! I know a lot of people have much harder jobs than I do, and I'm honestly just really thankful to be working. 

So I try to just push through it, you know? I wouldn't say I'm... like, falling apart over it or anything like that. It's just maybe a little stressful sometimes, mostly because I care so much about doing a good job and keeping people safe. But I handle it! I really do. 

I hope I'm not making it sound like I can't handle my responsibilities. I just don't want to come across like I'm whining or making a huge deal out of nothing. Is... is that an okay answer? Please let me know if I'm not explaining myself right.
Do you feel like you're checking the car over and over because you need to control every aspect of the ride or because you're afraid of what might happen if something goes wrong?

Um... well, it's definitely not about trying to control everything. I really hope it doesn't seem like I'm some sort of control freak! I just... I want to be a good driver. It's really just about being afraid of what could happen if I miss something. 

Like I was saying before—and I'm really sorry to keep bringing it up, I hope I'm not boring you—but that's why I keep going around the car, checking the tires, the lights, the doors, the meter, the paperwork... just over and over. And taking the pictures on my phone. It's just because I'm so worried something will go wrong and someone will get hurt because of me. 

That's why I have to restart the whole check if it doesn't feel right, even when I know the passengers are waiting and I'm already running late. I feel terrible about making them wait, I really do. I just... I can't shake that fear of something bad happening if I don't check it perfectly. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question okay.
Do you think you would still feel the need to check the car if someone you trusted, like a mechanic, had already checked it for you?

Um... wow, that's a really good question. I actually haven't really been in that situation, since I'm always the one picking the cab up for my shift. But... um... I hope this doesn't make me sound completely unreasonable, or like I don't trust professionals, because I really do respect mechanics! 

But I think... I think I would probably still have to check it. 

I would never want to insult them or make them feel bad, I promise. It's just that... if I'm the one driving, and I didn't do my own routine myself, I just wouldn't get that feeling that it's safe. I'd be driving the passengers around and just thinking, "What if the mechanic got distracted? What if they missed a tire, and this is the one time something terrible happens?" 

So I'd probably still have to do the whole thing myself anyway, just to be sure. I'm really sorry, I know that probably sounds so silly and disrespectful to whoever checked it. Does... does that make me sound awful? I really don't mean to be difficult, I just wouldn't be able to shake that feeling.
